chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Abu Jamila, from Simak ibn Harb, from Tamim ibn Tarafa, that two men recognized a camel, so each one of them produced evidence, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made it out to both of them.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (a title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.بِعِيرًا: a camel or a group of camels

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve a dispute when two men claimed the same camel with equal evidence?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) judicial wisdom in applying the principle of *Qasam* (division) or shared ownership when two parties present equally valid claims to a single indivisible asset. It serves as a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for resolving ambiguous property disputes through equitable distribution rather than arbitrary selection. The ruling underscores the Imam’s commitment to justice (*Adl*) by ensuring neither claimant is unjustly deprived of their due share.
